subject: RE: Multi-tenant controls — rate limits, quotas, and tiering (Acme)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sli@acme.com>, Jason Park <jason.park@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Multi-tenant controls — rate limits, quotas, and tiering (Acme)

Hi Sarah & Jason —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap from our side with the pieces we agreed to validate and the proposed next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points you mentioned
- Per-tenant rate spikes during BizOps jobs that blow past your shared pool and cause noisy neighbors for other teams.
- Need hard per-customer token/requests quotas plus soft throttles for bursty traffic.
- Want routing policies so premium customers hit higher-capacity pools and fall back to lower-cost models during congestion.
- Regulatory teams need clear audit trails and per-tenant metrics for billing and compliance.

Current stack & constraints (what you told us)- Primary product API sits in front of multiple model endpoints (self-hosted + cloud).
- Requests are proxied through an internal gateway that doesn't apply per-tenant shaping today.
- You have a 3rd-party billing system that requires per-customer usage CSVs / daily syncs.

Success criteria for an initial pilot (mutually agreed)- Enforce per-tenant request and token quotas without adding >50ms median latency.
- Route 95% of premium customers to dedicated pool during peak windows.
- Deliver audit log export (S3) with per-tenant keys and 7-day retention.

Action items we own
1) Draft a configuration example for per-customer quotas + soft throttles (attachment: Acme-MAP-2026.pdf).
2) Show a routing policy prototype that maps tiers -> pools (Vivek to own a short demo).
3) Share SLA wording for dedicated routing and fallbacks (attachment: redwood-sla-draft.docx).

Action items we asked you to confirm
- Desired tier definitions ("Premium", "Standard", "Economy") and rules for overflow.
- Approximate peak RPS per tier and typical burst duration.
- Who on your side will own billing CSV verification (Jason?).

Proposed timeline- Week 1: configuration draft + routing prototype video (this week).
- Week 2: 30-minute working session to validate policy JSON and quotas.
- Week 3: pilot run with one Premium customer for 48 hours.

If this looks right I'll attach the MAP and SLA draft and schedule the working session for next week.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Multi-tenant controls — rate limits, quotas, and tiering (Acme)

Thanks Laura — this is a great recap. A few clarifications:

- Tier definitions: confirm Premium (SLA + dedicated pool), Standard (shared pool with higher weight), Economy (best-effort). We'll send an official doc but that matches our intent.
- Peak RPS: Premium ~ 120 RPS during business hours (bursts to 350 for <5m), Standard ~ 40 RPS bursts to 120, Economy less than 10.
- Billing verify: Jason will own the daily CSV ingestion and double-check fields.

Can Vivek show an example of how the system behaves when Premium exceeds dedicated pool (i.e., how auto-fallback and rate-limiting interplay)? Also please confirm the latency budget — our SREs want to keep p50 < 60ms for inference.

We'll review the attachments and loop in Security if needed for audit requirements.

— Sarah
Sarah Li
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corporation
sli@acme.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme tiering clarifications & demo prep

Laura — copying internal notes from Sarah's reply and my take on the demo.

Notes
- Latency budget: p50 < 60ms target (we should benchmark with their average prompt length; ask for token distribution).
- Routing policy: implement a 'strict-reserve' for Premium where dedicated pool capacity is reserved up to X RPS; overflow -> queued soft-fallback (tiered model variant) with configurable drop policy.
- Quotas: daily token caps per tenant + sliding-window burst allowance (e.g., 1m/5m/1h windows).
- Billing: produce daily per-tenant CSV with columns {tenant_id, date, tokens, requests, routing_pool}. Jason wants schema validation on ingestion.

Demo plan for Vivek
1) Small recording showing: Premium routed to dedicated pool + simulated spike -> automatic fallback to cheaper model + telemetry view showing per-tenant throttle counts.
2) Show config JSON for quota windows and example of rate-limit response (429 + Retry-After header) vs soft-throttle behavior (queue + warning header).

Monica — can you prepare a short note on how our audit logs map to their S3 export and retention policy? Keep it to one page for Security.

I'll take the configuration draft and produce the initial policy JSON. Laura, I'll attach the sample policy to the working session invite.

-rishi
